patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..8483c52 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -5,7 +5,6 @@ def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Visible tests BEFORE fix: 'visible tests passed' exit 0 (weak tests pass despite bug). 2) Dumped report before fix: 6 lines with 101/102 duplicated under both Acme customers, total 290 -- reproduces both reported symptoms. 3) Applied one-line fix (match by customer id). 4) run_tests.py after fix -> 'visible tests passed'. 5) Report after fix: 4 lines, total 165, both distinct Zenith orders retained. 6) git diff shows exactly the patch above.
cause: orders_for_customer matched by display name instead of unique customer identity; customers id 1 and id 2 share the name 'Acme', so each Acme order was attributed to both. Fix matches order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]. Not a duplicate-row problem: orders 103/104 are genuinely separate and are preserved rather than de-duplicated.
